newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bond bears out again on U.S., France news.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bond bears out again on U.S., France news.

text.p: Continental European bond markets including Belgium would likely fall on Friday after a rise in a U.S. business sentiment index sent Bunds tumbling, OLO dealers said.
Fears that the French deficit was out of control would also weigh, they said.

French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said in his first policy speech in parliament on Thursday first indications were that the budgetary shortfall inherited from the previous government was serious, but a mini-budget would not be in place before autumn.
On the other side of the Atlantic, Treasuries moved lower on news the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June business activity index rose to 25.2 from 1.6 in May against expectations of 7.3.

The news took the Bund FDBc1 future from levels over 101.40 to levels around 101.10 by 1500 GMT. One Belgian OLO trader said he believed the future could now break through support at 101. "We will break the figure," he said.

Belgian OLO futures BGBc1 followed suit, turning from positive to negative territory, pushing the yield on the benchmark 10-year up to 5.84 from 5.78 earlier in the session. The 10-year yield had ended Wednesday at 5.80 percent.

As is usual, Belgian bonds slightly lagged the down move in Bunds, with the spread tightening to seven from eight basis points. One trader said he believed the levels were justified. "I think we can stay between seven and nine basis points," he said.

He said he did not personally believe the U.S. data was enough on its own to prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its July 1/2 meeting, but the trend for now was down. "The next stop will be 100.60 on the Bund," he said.
"The bears are out again," he added.
